**Headline:** The business Manage Card stops laying off whichever staff member happened to be hired last: it now lists every member employed at that business, one row each with its own `[ Move ]` and `[ Lay off ]`, and an explicit confirm step quoting the exact coins and reputation before anything is charged.

## Problem statement

The Manage Card dialog is the only door for letting business staff go, but it never asks *who*: both `[ Move staff ]` and `[ Lay off ]` act on `employedStaff[employedStaff.length - 1]` (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:926,944`). A business holding two or more members therefore exposes one control per action that silently targets the newest hire, and the lay-off executes with no cost preview and no confirmation.

## Users

- **Main Street player with a staffed business (hands-on)** — employs several specialists and wants to change the team.
  - As a player, I want to see everyone employed at this business in one place, with their effect and salary, so that I can decide which specialist is worth keeping.
  - As a player, I want to press a button that belongs to the member I mean, so that I never fire the wrong specialist by accident.
  - As a player, I want the exact coins and reputation the lay-off will charge shown before I commit, so that a €500/turn executive cannot end my run unannounced.
- **Main Street player chasing business efficiency (economy-focused)** — compares each member's salary against its local effect.
  - As a player, I want each row's salary next to the member's effect, so that I can judge the cut by its savings.
- **Game designer / QA** — needs both lay-off doors to state one rule the same way.
  - As QA, I want the quoted cost to equal the charge that lands, so that a skill discount or a clamp cannot silently diverge.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Manage Card dialog renders an **employed-staff section** with exactly one row per member employed at that slot (`employedAtSlot === slotIndex`) and nothing else — management-company staff never appear. Each row shows the member's name, its role/benefit summary (from a shared formatter, not a UI-invented string) and its effective per-turn salary resolved through `computeStaffSalaryCost(getSalaryScopeSkills(member), member.ongoingCost)`.
- Rows are ordered deterministically (hire order, oldest first) and the panel sizes itself from the row count: at the maximum employment capacity of a business (`level + 1`) every row, button and the sell/close/cancel row are fully visible with no clipping or overlap; with no member employed the section renders nothing at all (today's empty-state behaviour).
- Each row carries `[ Move ]` and `[ Lay off ]` addressed to **that** member. `[ Move ]` hands the member's id to `beginStaffMove`, keeping the existing `moving-staff` choreography, the 1-action cost and the per-member destination list from `buildMoveStaffAffordance(state, member.id)` in its hover tooltip. `[ Lay off ]` opens the confirm step for that member only. Because the per-row labels are short, the section states both costs once in its own line (`Move: 1 action · Lay off: 1 turn's salary + reputation`) so neither cost is hidden behind a tooltip. No control in the dialog acts on "the most recently hired" member implicitly.
- The confirm step is an overlay quoting the member's name, one turn's salary in coins (clamped at 0) and the reputation cost from the shared `layOffReputationCost(salary)` — the single formula decided in MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA and **not re-derived here**. `[ Confirm ]` executes `letGoStaffCommand` through the undo manager (the lay-off stays undoable); `[ Cancel ]` changes nothing and returns to the member list.
- After a confirmed lay-off the dialog stays open and re-renders in place: the row disappears, the panel shrinks to fit, and once the last member leaves the staff section disappears while sell/close/cancel keep working. Rows are addressed by **member id** and resolved against `state.staffCards` at click time, so a stale row (the member is already gone, e.g. after an undo) re-renders and flashes feedback instead of acting on a shifted index.
- The activity-log entry and confirmation flash quote the charges actually applied — e.g. `Laid off <name> (−<coins> coins, −<reputation> reputation)` — replacing the hard-coded "−1 salary, −1 reputation" strings.
- Unit tests cover the pure model: membership filtering for the slot, ordering, per-row salary, coin clamp, reputation quote per row, id-addressing/staleness and the empty case; a test pins the confirm step's quoted cost to the effect of `letGoStaffMember()` (quoted == charged) including a discounted-salary member.
- Browser/render tests cover: no affordance when nobody is employed; two employed members produce two rows with two `[ Move ]` and two `[ Lay off ]` controls; the *first* row's `[ Lay off ]` lays off the *first* member (the regression this item exists for) and the *first* row's `[ Move ]` targets the first member; confirm/cancel behaviour; in-place refresh after a lay-off; the section disappearing when the last member leaves; and sell/close/cancel still working.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (`docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` D.4.2 §5, `docs/game/card-catalog.md`, `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`, `src/README.md`).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A player who has hired several specialists at one business can finally pick which one leaves — seeing each member's effect, salary and the exact lay-off price first — instead of a single button that always fires the newest hire.

## Constraints

- **Blocked by MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA.** That item lands the salary-scaled reputation rule in `letGoStaffMember()` and exports `layOffReputationCost(salary)`. This item consumes that helper and the same lay-off confirm standard; the formula is not re-litigated here.
- **One confirm step, two doors.** The confirm step is being built for the roster by its child **MS-0MWC9PCSB001MCMQ**. This item reuses the shared confirm content builder and cost helpers rather than writing a second quoting implementation; if that child lands the confirm local to the roster dialog, this item factors the shared content builder out and both call it.
- **No engine change.** No new command and no new persisted state. Membership is derived from `state.staffCards` on open and after each action; lay-off stays `letGoStaffCommand` (snapshot → undoable) and relocation stays `moveStaffCommand` (1 action).
- **Address by id, never by index.** `letGoStaffCommand(state, index)` is index-based, so a click resolves the row's member id to a current index at click time and refuses when the member is gone.
- **Pure model first.** Row building, salary/cost resolution and confirm copy live in a Phaser-free module so they are unit-testable; the overlay only draws.
- **One source of truth for figures.** Salaries come from `computeStaffSalaryCost`/`getSalaryScopeSkills`; the lay-off reputation cost from `layOffReputationCost`; the move destinations and 1-action cost from `buildMoveStaffAffordance`. No UI- or model-local arithmetic.
- **Overlay kit only.** `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton` / `dismissOverlay`, every element parented into `s.hudContainer`, depths 199/200/201, everything tracked in `s.overlayObjects`, instant appearance (reduced-motion safe), suppressed in `replayMode`/headless runs. No new art — rows are text plus kit buttons.
- **Don't touch the mechanics.** Sell, close, cancel and the move/destination flow keep their current behaviour and costs; only the staff section and its confirm step change.
- **Localisation.** New user-visible strings follow the `HUD_TOOLTIP_I18N_KEYS` / `HUD_TOOLTIP_STRINGS` English-bundle pattern where a key fits; overlay-only labels may follow the journal/undo-warning literal-string precedent.
- **UK English**, no `CHANGELOG.md` edits (managed by the release pipeline).

## Existing state

- The Manage Card dialog (`showSellConfirmation`, `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:690-975`) is a fixed 480×410 panel: card info, sale value, a close-cost line, `[ Sell ]` / `[ Close ]` / `[ Cancel ]` at `panelY + 265`, then a single `Employed here: <names>` line (`+305`) and one `[ Move staff (1 action) ]` (`+352, centerX − 110`) plus one `[ Lay off ]` (`+352, centerX + 110`).
- Both staff handlers target the newest hire: `const moveTarget = employedStaff[employedStaff.length - 1]` (`:926`) and `const target = employedStaff[employedStaff.length - 1]` (`:944`). Neither asks for confirmation.
- Membership today: `allStaff.map((member, index) => ({ member, index })).filter(({ member }) => member.employedAtSlot === slotIndex)` (`:700-704`) — the `index` is the `state.staffCards` index `letGoStaffCommand` needs.
- `letGoStaffMember()` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:1513`) removes the member, charges one turn's effective salary clamped at 0 and a flat **1** reputation, then deregisters it from the business's `employedStaff`. `letGoStaffCommand()` (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts:903`) wraps it in a snapshot.
- `buildMoveStaffAffordance(state, staffId?)` (`src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts:613`) already accepts an explicit member id, resolves legal destinations through `canMoveStaffOnBusiness` and rejects illegal starts; today the dialog always passes the newest hire. `onMoveStaffClick(staffId)` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts:362`) accepts any employed member's id.
- Overlay precedents: `showStorylineJournalDialog()` (`:1655`) row list with empty state and replay short-circuit; `showUndoChallengeWarningDialog()` (`:1227`) is the confirm/cancel shape; `MainStreetLoanSelectorModel` + `MainStreetLoanOverlay` is the pure-model-plus-row-list pair; `showBuyAndPlacePremiumDialog()` (`:994`) the cost-quote-then-confirm structure.
- `formatEmployedStaffSummary()` (`src/MainStreetFormatting.ts:452`) already renders per-member `• <name> (<types>) — <description>` lines for the street tooltip — the shared role/benefit text the rows should reuse rather than re-invent.
- The Manage Card only opens for an owned, non-sold, managing-phase slot (`onSellCard` → `showSellConfirmation`), and its handlers carry defensive legality guards; nothing here changes that gating.
- Tests asserting the current behaviour: `tests/main-street/manage-card-dialog.browser.test.ts` (lay-off with one member, expects −1 reputation and dialog dismissal; no-affordance empty case), plus `letGoStaffMember`-based expectations in `MainStreetApplicant.test.ts`, `staff-skill-scope-gate.test.ts`, `staff-business-type-matching.test.ts` and `MainStreetIntegration.test.ts`.

## Desired change

1. **Pure model** (new `src/MainStreetBusinessStaff.ts`, or a builder added to the roster module MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA creates): `buildBusinessStaffRows(state, slotIndex)` → ordered rows `{ memberId, name, roleSummary, salary, layOffCoins, layOffReputation, moveEnabled, moveDestinations }`, plus `businessStaffIsEmpty(state, slotIndex)`; reuses `layOffReputationCost`, `computeStaffSalaryCost`, `getSalaryScopeSkills`, `buildMoveStaffAffordance` and a shared `formatStaffRoleLine(member)` factored out of `formatEmployedStaffSummary`.
2. **Confirm content builder** (pure): `buildLayOffConfirmContent(row)` → title/body lines for name, coins and reputation, so the copy and arithmetic are shared with the Company Roster's confirm step rather than duplicated.
3. **Staff rows in the Manage Card** (`showSellConfirmation`): replace the single `Employed here` line and the two fixed buttons with a cost line plus a row list (name · role/benefit · salary, `[ Move ]`, `[ Lay off ]` per row), panel height computed from the row count, and an in-place re-render after a lay-off or a stale-row refusal.
4. **Confirm step**: pressing a row's `[ Lay off ]` shows the confirm overlay (confirm → `letGoStaffCommand` via the undo manager → re-render; cancel → back to the rows untouched).
5. **Copy**: log/flash strings quote the applied charges instead of the literal `−1 salary, −1 reputation`.
6. **Docs and tests** as per the acceptance criteria; the existing one-member lay-off browser test is updated to go through the confirm step.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — `showSellConfirmation()`: staff row list, per-row `[ Move ]`/`[ Lay off ]`, confirm step, in-place re-render, panel sizing.
- `src/MainStreetBusinessStaff.ts` — **new** pure model: slot membership, ordering, row salary/role text, coin/reputation quotes, id-addressing, confirm content.
- `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — factor `formatStaffRoleLine(member)` out of `formatEmployedStaffSummary()` so tooltip, roster and Manage Card share one role/benefit text.
- `src/MainStreetRoster.ts` — the module MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA creates with `layOffReputationCost()`; add the business-staff row builder here if the company roster's row shape fits (preferred), otherwise a sibling module importing the same cost helper.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — `beginStaffMove(memberId)` from a row (reference; unchanged signature).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts` — `onMoveStaffClick(staffId)` (reference; already per-member).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — `buildMoveStaffAffordance` (reference) plus any new i18n keys/strings for row and confirm copy.
- `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` / `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — `letGoStaffCommand` / `letGoStaffMember` (reference; formula owned by MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA).
- `tests/main-street/business-staff-selection.test.ts` — **new** unit tests: rows, ordering, salary/cost quotes, coin clamp, stale-row handling, quoted == charged.
- `tests/main-street/manage-card-dialog.browser.test.ts` — extend: multiple members, per-row lay-off/move targeting, confirm/cancel, re-render, empty section, sell/close/cancel intact; update the one-member lay-off expectation.
- `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` — D.4.2 §5: lay-off from the Manage Card states member selection and the confirm step.
- `docs/game/card-catalog.md` — the shared staff-rules line (lay-off selection + cost).
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — Manage Card staff rows, confirm step, empty state, input behavior.
- `src/README.md` — the Manage Card staff-rows section replacing the current "press [ Lay off ]" paragraph.

## Related work

This item applies the same rule and standard to business staff and records the follow-up (Q6) that raised it.

- Docs: `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` (D.4.2 §5, D.4.8), `docs/game/card-catalog.md`, `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — the wrong member leaves anyway.** The current bug is an off-by-selection; a row UI could repeat it if it kept index-based targeting, or if the rows drifted from `state.staffCards` after an undo. *Mitigation:* rows carry member ids resolved at click time, a stale row refuses and re-renders, and a browser test asserts the first row lays off the first member under two-employee state.
- **Risk — quoted cost ≠ charged cost.** A discount, clamp or future formula change could make the confirm step lie. *Mitigation:* the quote comes from the same helpers the command uses (`computeStaffSalaryCost`, `layOffReputationCost`), and a unit test pins quote == charge for a discounted member.
- **Risk — panel growth breaks the dialog at capacity.** Six rows in a fixed 480×410 panel would overlap the sell/close buttons. *Mitigation:* height is derived from the row count and a browser test asserts no overlap at `level + 1` members.
- **Risk — scope creep back into the roster or into move mechanics.** *Mitigation:* the Company Roster's overlay stays MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA's; only the shared cost helper, role-text formatter and confirm copy are reused, and the move command/cost/phase are untouched.
- **Risk — the dialog stays open across a stale state.** Keeping it open after a lay-off is a new behaviour for this dialog. *Mitigation:* every re-render is derived from `state.staffCards`, clicks re-resolve by id, and `refreshAll()` remains the single refresh path.
- **Assumption:** the member list shows one business's employees (the managed slot), not the whole roster — the roster door is the Company Roster's job.
- **Assumption:** row order is hire order (oldest first), matching the roster's ordering decision, so rows do not reshuffle after a lay-off.
- **Assumption:** `[ Move ]` keeps its 1-action cost and its existing `moving-staff` destination-picking flow; the dialog closes on `[ Move ]` exactly as today, so no confirm step is added to relocation.
- **Assumption:** lay-off availability is unchanged (no phase or coin gate); the coin cost clamps at 0 and the reputation cost floors the run's reputation at 0, as today.
- **Assumption:** the confirm step can share its copy with the Company Roster's confirm through a pure builder even if the two overlays draw it separately — no shared rendering framework is introduced.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "How does the player choose which member to let go? — A. one row per employed member in the Manage Card dialog, each with its own `[ Lay off ]` (mirrors the Company Roster); B. select a row, then one shared `[ Lay off ]` button; C. a separate lay-off picker sub-dialog." **Recommended:** A — reuses the row-list + per-row-action structure the Company Roster is standardising, so both lay-off doors look the same.
  - Answer (producer): "A". Source: interactive reply.
  - Final: A — one row per employed member, each row owning its own `[ Lay off ]`.
  - Research: the dialog already filters exactly this set (`employedAtSlot === slotIndex`, `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:700-704`); the roster's per-row `[ Lay off ]` is the AC set in MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA; `showStorylineJournalDialog` (`:1655`) supplies the row-list overlay precedent.
- Q2: "The same dialog's `[ Move staff ]` button also acts on the most recently hired member. Unify? — A. leave move-staff as-is and record the divergence; B. each row gains `[ Move ]` alongside `[ Lay off ]` (per-member move selection, here); C. rows gain only `[ Lay off ]` here and per-member move selection becomes its own item." **Recommended:** C — the move path has its own `moving-staff` phase and destination picking, so folding it in doubles the scope.
  - Answer (producer): "B". Source: interactive reply.
  - Final: B — each row carries `[ Move ]` and `[ Lay off ]`; per-member move selection is in scope for this item.
  - Research: the engine and controller already accept a member id (`onMoveStaffClick(staffId)`, `moveStaffCommand`, `buildMoveStaffAffordance(state, staffId?)` whose doc comment says "the Manage-Card dialog passes the member the player chose"), so per-row `[ Move ]` needs no engine work — only the dialog's target selection changes. Far cheaper than the recommended option assumed.
- Q3: "Where does the cost-preview/confirm step live? — A. a separate small confirm dialog quoting name, coins and reputation; B. an in-panel confirm state where the pressed row's button becomes `[ Confirm ]` / `[ Cancel ]`." **Recommended:** A — one confirm component shared with the Company Roster's lay-off, so the quoted cost cannot diverge between the two doors.
  - Answer (producer): "A". Source: interactive reply.
  - Final: A — separate confirm overlay with `[ Confirm ]` / `[ Cancel ]`.
  - Research: `showUndoChallengeWarningDialog` (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:1227`) and `showBuyAndPlacePremiumDialog` (`:994`) are the existing confirm-overlay precedents; MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA's roster AC sets the same confirm step for management-company members.

## Problem

`.pi/test-config.json` declares named test `groups`, and `run_tests.py`'s changed-scope selection is **group-first**: `changed_scope_selection()` returns the winning group's commands and never also runs the changed files' own tests (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, `select_group_from_changed_files`). Two consequences surfaced while implementing `MS-0MWBWKZ1G006IBH2` (Staff Pile):

1. **Changed test files can be skipped.** A slice that edits `src/layouts/*.json` + `src/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts` wins the `hand-bottom-anchor-browser` group, whose command runs only `tests/main-street/hand-bottom-anchor.browser.test.ts` — so the *changed* `tests/main-street/MainStreetLayoutAnchors.browser.test.ts` and `tests/main-street/tutorial-layout-resolution.test.ts` never ran in changed scope. A knowingly-wrong assertion in the new anchor test passed the finish gate and was only caught by the dev-push full suite.
2. **No group covers several frequently-touched modules.** Nothing matches `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStaffPile.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts`, `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts`, `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` or `src/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts`, so their tests are only selected by convention mapping — and any group that matches one *other* changed file (e.g. `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts`) takes precedence and replaces that selection (a renderer slice ran `webgl-renderer-clipping.browser.test.ts` and nothing else).

## Desired change

- Union, don't replace: when a group matches, also run the convention-mapped/individually-changed test files (or at minimum every changed test file), so editing a test can never escape the changed-scope gate.
- Add or extend project groups so the Main Street renderer/HUD/layout modules map to their own tests (layout anchor + tutorial resolution, HUD tooltips, staff pile).
- Add a regression test for the union rule (a changed test file outside the winning group's `paths` must still be executed).

## Notes

- Repository boundary: `.pi/test-config.json` and `skill/test/` are agent infrastructure — this item exists so the change is made deliberately, not as a side effect of a feature slice.
- Evidence: child comments on `MS-0MWC7NU7W006ZI3X` (false-positive anchor assertion) and `MS-0MWC7Z6OF008J0PP` (webgl group selected for renderer changes).
- Discovered from `MS-0MWBWKZ1G006IBH2`.

The competitive HUD scoreboard draws each seat's row text in that seat's raw persisted colour (`MainStreetRendererCompetitiveHud.ts`, `row.colour ?? NEUTRAL_ROW_COLOUR`). The colour-blind-safe palette includes the Okabe–Ito black (`#000000`), so a seat assigned that hue can render an unreadable row on the dark HUD.

Discovered while fixing the same defect in the Turn Summary tab strip (MS-0MWBWRITL0089GGJ): the shared helper `ensureReadableSeatColour()` (and `contrastRatio` / `parseHexColour`) now lives in `src/MainStreetSeatColours.ts`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A competitive HUD scoreboard row whose seat colour falls below WCAG AA contrast against the HUD background is lightened toward white via `ensureReadableSeatColour()`, so the row label is always readable.
- A seat colour that already clears the ratio is drawn unchanged (exact caller string), preserving seat identity.
- Unit/browser coverage pins the black-seat case on the HUD.
- All existing tests pass.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererCompetitiveHud.ts` — resolve the row text colour through `ensureReadableSeatColour()`
- `tests/main-street/competitive-hud-colour.test.ts` — extend with the legibility case

## Impact

No competitive player loses a scoreboard row to an unreadable seat colour.
